description: The round-2 FIND-002 fix makes isBorrowerEligibleWithReputationGate REACHABLE from lending-orchestrator.mjs's runLockedIssuance (step 6), but the wiring reads the wrong field name for the borrower's ERC-8004 identity, so the composed gate can NEVER succeed for a real borrower once a lender actually configures thresholds -- the exact scenario G3 exists to serve. lending-orchestrator.mjs:392 calls isBorrowerEligibleWithReputationGate(..., { borrowerAgentId: freshBorrower.agentId, ...(deps.reputationGate||{}) }, ...) -- reading `freshBorrower.agentId` (camelCase). But the ONLY place a real citizen registry row's ERC-8004 identity is ever written is skills/self/spawn/lib/child-spec.js:65 (`spec.agent_id = agentId;`) and skills/self/spawn/lib/spawn-orchestrator.mjs:680 (`agent_id: identityResult.agentId,`) -- both snake_case `agent_id`, confirmed as the deliberately tested, canonical schema by skills/self/spawn/lib/__tests__/spawn-orchestrator.test.mjs:191/538 and __tests__/child-spec-erc8004.test.js:37/66/85 (all assert `.agent_id`, never `.agentId`). wake-gate.mjs's buildDefaultGetCitizen (the real production getCitizen closure) does `return { ...citizen, balanceUsd };` -- a straight spread of the raw registry row, performing no snake_case-to-camelCase normalization anywhere in this repo (repo-wide grep for `.agentId`/`"agentId"` on a citizen/registry object returns zero hits outside this one buggy call site and its own test). Consequence: in production, `freshBorrower.agentId` is ALWAYS `undefined` for every real citizen. reputation-gate.mjs:32 (`if (!borrowerAgentId) return { eligible: false, reason: "no_borrower_agent_id" };`) is the documented, INTENTIONAL fail-closed branch for exactly this case ("a caller bug, not a network outage" per its own header comment) -- so the moment ANY lender configures minScore>0 or minJobCount>0 (the design spec's own stated G3 goal, §1: "閾値設定時に実績不足 borrower が弾かれる"), EVERY borrower is rejected with reason:"no_borrower_agent_id", not just borrowers with genuinely insufficient reputation. This is strictly worse than round-1's FIND-002 (unreachable dead code): the gate is now reachable but functionally inverted -- it blocks 100% of real borrowers the instant it is turned on, silently defeating the feature's entire stated purpose while looking, from every green test, like it works. No test in this feature's suite catches this: lending-orchestrator.test.mjs's own FIND-002 wiring test (line 225-246) injects a fully-mocked `deps.reputationGateFn` (never the real `passesOnchainReputationGate` default) and its own inline comment at line 241 explicitly acknowledges `freshBorrower.agentId` is undefined in its fixture, dismissing it as "a separate, future data-plumbing concern" rather than the load-bearing defect it actually is; the 'defaults to real gate' test (line 248-253) never configures a threshold, so it short-circuits before ever reading borrowerAgentId and cannot exercise this branch either.
